answer_text:
The parameter interval is not stated, so the integral depends on the chosen limits. Let \(t\) run from \(t_0\) to \(t_1\).

Given

\[
x=a(t-\sin t), \qquad y=a(1-\cos t),
\]

we have

\[
dx=a(1-\cos t)\,dt, \qquad dy=a\sin t\,dt.
\]

Therefore,

\[
x\,dy-y\,dx
=
a^2\big[(t-\sin t)\sin t-(1-\cos t)^2\big]\,dt.
\]

Simplify the bracket:

\[
\begin{aligned}
(t-\sin t)\sin t-(1-\cos t)^2
&=t\sin t-\sin^2 t-(1-2\cos t+\cos^2 t)\\
&=t\sin t-\sin^2 t-1+2\cos t-\cos^2 t\\
&=t\sin t+2\cos t-2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus,

\[
x\,dy-y\,dx
=
a^2\left(t\sin t+2\cos t-2\right)\,dt.
\]

Now integrate:

\[
\int a^2\left(t\sin t+2\cos t-2\right)\,dt
=
a^2\left(-t\cos t+\sin t+2\sin t-2t\right).
\]

So

\[
\int (x\,dy-y\,dx)
=
a^2\left(3\sin t-t\cos t-2t\right).
\]

Hence, for limits \(t=t_0\) to \(t=t_1\),

\[
\int_{t_0}^{t_1}(x\,dy-y\,dx)
=
a^2\left[3\sin t-t\cos t-2t\right]_{t_0}^{t_1}.
\]

If the intended curve is one full cycloid arch, \(0\le t\le 2\pi\), then

\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^{2\pi}(x\,dy-y\,dx)
&=
a^2\left[3\sin t-t\cos t-2t\right]_0^{2\pi}\\
&=
a^2\left(0-2\pi-4\pi-0\right)\\
&=-6\pi a^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus, for the standard one-arch orientation given by increasing \(t\),

\[
\boxed{-6\pi a^2}
\]
